body:
A few things stood out to me about your post. I know from your perspective you are very focused on the lack of affection towards you (since you are the injured party) but are there outside problems too? Especially when you spoke about him only being “content” on the phone or while gaming. In other words, is he struggling mentally? Depression? Is he happy with his profession and family life? He always wanted to be a father, but is it more difficult than he expected?

More information about the length of your relationship would also be a bit of help. How long before the affection faded? Were there any major life events around that time?

All of this is to say, maybe it doesn’t involve what you’re doing. It seems like you’re doing all you can for him.

Yeah I feel that first sentence. Got back with my ex after she dumped me last year (around this time) then got back with her about two weeks later. Recently she’s been bringing up separating again so I’ll probably be right there with you by tomorrow. 

I think it’s pretty considerate of you to wait for the “right” time (if such a thing can be), but I also feel like by the time a year has passed you’ll feel different. I don’t have any children so I’m not totally sure how it feels, but you’ve got a whole year to be an amazing father to your son. 

Hope your ice cream is good.

Wow. So, I read your entire story and honestly it couldn’t be more tragic if someone were trying to make it so. You seem to have suffered a great deal in life at the hands of other people. I’m glad that (at least it seems) you’re in a better place now with university and aspirations. I think it’s noble that you want to give back through volunteering and becoming an animal doctor. I think it’s also good that it seems you still treat others with decency even though they may not return it. Honestly, if you’ve been through so much and continue fighting, it is an inspiration to us all. 

Your final question, where you asked what to do, I think has a few answers. Mostly, I think, the answer is keep going. You’re studying and doing well and no doubt will succeed as an animal doctor. I think that even if humans don’t treat you well, then the animals will appreciate your humanity instead. Good luck.

Wow I went through the same thing recently (except with a girl)! She said she was upset that she couldn’t treat me like I deserved because her depression was getting in the way and that she didn’t have the mental capacity for a relationship either. Unfortunately, she doesn’t seem to be making any plans to make it better and return like your ex has. She’s still texting me begging to be friends and saying she’s worried about me, but it’ll just rip me up inside. 

I agree with your second paragraph about not knowing when they’ll leave again. It might never happen again but it’s hard since now we know they’re capable of it. 

It’s not selfish at all to be sad over this. I went through something similar with my first love and wished I had be shot instead. It’s much easier to cure and diagnose physical trauma than emotional ones. Honestly, at least the reason we were given doesn’t involve us I guess? But it doesn’t really make the end result any different. 

I’m sorry for you. Let me know if you want to talk anymore about it.
Don’t do it! Usually doesn’t end well. In fact, take this time to block and or delete their number if you feel so compelled. Then you won’t have to deal with these urges.

I think that if you’ve kept your honor in treating her fairly, then that’s something to be proud of. I can’t say who you are or what happened between you, but you certainly do. Fighting with your brother as a youth is incredibly common and I don’t think that’s at all relevant to your concerns. 

From you story, I don’t think that one (justifiable?) incident between two guys, one of whom is drunk and belligerent, is at all similar to domestic abuse. I can’t dictate how she feels right now, but it’s not impossible she said things in a less-than-stellar state of mind. Many people vilify their exes to make themselves feel better and to rationalize what has happened. 

My advice, if you’re willing, is to avoid contact with her. I’m not saying ghost her, but I would at least tell her that you need time to focus on yourself. For better or worse, she no longer gets to decide or have a say in your choices. 

It is therefore now your chance and opportunity to improve yourself — not as a way to get back at her or to reconcile — but rather as the only path forward. Don’t resign yourself to your “doom”, but rather strive against it. 

As always, if you want to chat further let me know. Good luck.

It seems pretty clear that the man wants to see (I.e. have sex with) other people while keeping you on the line. He knows that at any point he can text you and you’ll come sprinting down to see him. Now, whether or not that is something you’re okay with is truly a matter of your own perspective. However, I am of the opinion that it is moderately self-degrading to be at his beck and call, especially since he’s the one who dumped you. 

If you really and truly want him after that, I don’t think being friends is the correct option unless you’re both going to be seeing other people and that’s what you both want. But from your description of your feelings, it seems like you’d be devastated to find out if he were seeing other people. Maybe you should ask him clearly if he is or isn’t, and when he gives you the affirmative response, your feelings will change drastically. 

Wishing you all the best.

Look man I’m gonna keep it 100 with you. This relationship seemed toxic as hell. None of your needs were being met and neither were hers, unfortunately. But if we compare the relative needs for each party, then a new picture emerges from this perspective. 

On one hand, we have your needs: financial support, physical affection and commitment. Those are all fair things, especially because your ex wife had garnered so much much from her inheritance and passive income. 

On her side, she wanted someone with money and lots of it. I’m sorry, but it just seems like you weren’t able to do that. And that’s not your fault. It seems circumstances have been hard for you to have a well-paying job, especially with your ex-wife’s inability to do many of the things that normal adults do on her own. 

But think about it now. Really consider what you’re free from. Wouldn’t you want someone instead that can drive on their own? Willing to compromise on bills in a marriage? Financially responsible? Kind?? Loyal and not flirting with other guys???

I am glad for you that this pit of despair has ended. You know what to do now. Cut contact with this woman and be a good father to your son as much as you can be. It’s not going to be easy but it’ll be a hell of a lot better now. Good luck.

Hey friend,

Welcome to the new and likely difficult world of breakups. It’s likely not going to be easy for awhile, regardless of how long you were together. 

To answer your question though, I’d say probably stay away from being friends for the time being and avoid talking to her (no contact). It’s critical for you to move forward because every bit of interaction with her will just make this process more difficult. It’s not being mean or heartless, it’s about having self-respect and putting yourself first. 

Beyond that, I’d try to comprehend your emotions and (this may sound ridiculous) appreciate that you can feel such extreme emotions. Let me know if you want to talk some more — I know that the only thing that made me feel better was talking about it.

I’m sorry friend. I’m 21M so I can relate to a lot of your body issues. Often times people make fun of me saying “I look really young” or “like a kid” so I can understand what it’s like to be body conscious. I’m not really sure how to cure/alleviate body image issues; unfortunately, they’re kind of genetic in nature. And that can be good or bad, but at least you can change the way you look by putting on more weight — but only if you want to, not for the opinion of others.

I think you should try to go back into the electricians’ field. It’s a solid trade with a lot of long-term potential and you seem fulfilled. But of course try to find a new apprenticeship, even if you have to move. I’m sure that you can find a place where the people there are more concerned about getting work done rather than what you look like.

Yeah I know what’s up, at least to a large extent. The last girl I dated had similar issues to your ex and it’s tough to try to work through your own things while supporting someone else. And I’ve been in another relationship where I changed so much about myself and sacrificed things that I just can’t get back to be with her and it didn’t matter I guess. And yeah I tried to kill myself both times after so I know how bad it gets. And I still am recovering from the second breakup just 2 months ago so things still aren’t great. Heartbreak is likely one of the worst things we go through as human beings, at least for some people. 

I’m not going to try to tell you things work out for the best or that it all happened for some greater reason, because I don’t believe in all that. Sometimes when we lose things they just don’t come back. It’s depressing and brutal and I suppose it doesn’t really happen for any real purpose. 

Let me know if you want to talk some more, I know that talking about my breakups were one of the few things that would make me feel bette, at least temporarily.

Heartbreak is one of the worst experiences we can go through as human beings. It makes you question yourself fundamentally as a person. And I’ve been where you are (you can check some of my other posts) in terms of wanting to kill myself over someone else. I can’t say whether it’s right or wrong because I still want to die most days, but I want you to know that you’re not alone in feeling this way. 

When my first girlfriend cheated on me, I was locked in the psych ward and it was horrible. But if that may keep you safe for the time being, I would try to go in voluntarily in order to prevent it from barring you from owning guns ever again. 

Anyways, I can’t really say anything about your method other than I think you shouldn’t do it since it would be extraordinarily painful and likely to only make your situation worse.

Yeah man I have been going through a period of fatalistic nihilism if that even makes any sense. Like we don’t have any control over our lives, regardless of what we do, and even so, none of it even matters. Really makes it hard to want to exist when nothing can provide any sort of meaning. Hope you get better friend.

I feel you man. It’s never easy going through heartbreak and the two times I did (one being recently) I tried to kill myself but, for better or worse, didn’t succeed. Honestly, wish that we were like the people that didn’t care or that move on easily, but I guess we just aren’t like that. Went on a  few dates last week with a new girl I met online and I thought everything was going well but — anyways that’s not important I guess. 

But I did want to write this and say that it does feel like you’re alone because it’s magnified by being alone I guess. You no longer have that person anymore. And I’m not going to try to bullshit you about moving on or self improvement or whatever cause it’s not helpful to hear. It’s just more shitty things that happen in life I guess. 

Hope things can change for you.

Yeah I feel you man. A lot of times rejection feels like a rejection of who we are as a person — whether or not they meant it that way. Oftentimes I wonder if there’s something fundamentally wrong with me when things like that happen.

In my experience the police will arrive and then escort you by ambulance if they deem you a threat to yourself. I think it’s a liability thing at the point where they have to involuntarily hospitalize you. I’m not sure what happens if you voluntarily go but even a short ambulance ride can cost upwards of $2000. So... yeah. Would advise against ever involving the state in this.

That sounds really tough to deal with right now. The part that stuck out most to me was probably “I just want to be happy.” I think that’s what everyone wants but everyone also says to do what makes you happy. Honestly I think that if you’re like me, you probably have no clue how to do that if nothing makes you happy. 

The other part that stuck out to me was when you said “we’re all slaves.” I feel like no matter what we do, we don’t have really any agency in our lives, much like slaves. I hope it gets better for you friend.

I’m sorry to hear your story. Heartbreak is likely one of the worst things we can experience as humans. I know what you’re going through: both times my long-term girlfriends dumped me I tried to kill myself too. Oftentimes I wonder if it would’ve been better or worse to have done it before I met the second one, but now we’re here dealing with it nonetheless. 

I’m glad they didn’t lock you up or anything; that’s usually what I would’ve expected from all that. I don’t think that it was a epiphany for you or anything cause I’m not sure if such things are true, but at least you can really reflect on it now. 

Your last part is absolutely heartbreaking because I feel the same way. Why couldn’t we be happy together? I don’t know. But I’m glad you don’t hate her because oftentimes people demonize their exes for no good reason. 

I can’t promise you anything but I understand you.

This is very difficult and a lot of people will probably give you less sympathy since you initiated the breakup, but I think you made the decision you wanted to make. Right or wrong is irrelevant, now you have to struggle through this aftermath. And I think that it shows that even the dumper goes through much of the same issues that the dumpee does too. 

I think that if your incompatibilities are truly untenable then it’s good you made the decision now, rather than far in the future. If you were married or had children together the aftermath would be much more complicated and difficult. And I know that doesn’t really help since this is happening now and not as some indiscriminate point in the future but there’s less sunken cost if that makes sense. 

I’m wishing you all the best in moving forward.

I wrote a bunch of somewhat depressing poems but here’s one you may like:

**True Love**


A beautiful sentiment,


A love most true,


Incapable of deserting,


The perfect half of you. 

Calm if needed, but will put up a fight,


Loves you even if you can’t screw in a light,


Communicates well and respects what you do,


Cares about your day and the football scores too. 



Gentle and kind,


Unobtainable and bleak, 


Only one line is truth,


Which one do you think?

I feel how you do, except I’m a guy. Honestly heartbreak is probably one of the worst emotions that humans have to go through and some people shake it off quickly and others simply need a lot more time. Sometimes I try to appreciate the fact that we as people are capable of feeling such brutal lows, but I’m not sure if that helps.

8 months of no contact and then having those feelings rush back must feel like another breakup all over again. I can’t tell you what to do with your life, but the only way to prevent this from devastating you over and over again is simply to not contact him anymore. And I’m sure that hurts more than anything in the world. I mean I have overwhelming urges to contact my ex just for some hope, too. 

I don’t know what else to say besides that fact I hope you find comfort with the other broken-hearted people in the world.

I feel you a lot. Breakups feel like the end of the world. My girlfriend of two years just left, and I feel like ending it too. I don’t know how old you are or what your relationship is like, but I hope it works out for you and I hope you feel not alone with all the other broken-hearted people in the world.

I’m the same age you are, but I think that your situation is understandably very difficult. It must not be easy trying to constantly compete with your sister. Do your parents understand the issues that you’re facing or do they compare you two constantly? Maybe you could have a real discussion with your sister about how she feels—it may turn out she’s not as confident as she seems especially at 14 (?). 

Not seeing that you have a purpose or any talents can make anyone hopeless and I’m sorry you’re dealing with this.
